Against The Judgment And Award Dated 24.04.2019 Passed
In Mvc No. 260/2017 On The File Of The Senior Civil Judge

Bailhongal, Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For
Compensation And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Futher Orders, This Day,
S.G. Pandit J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for orders, it is taken up for final disposal, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.

2. The claimants are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 24.04.2019 passed in MVC No.260/2017 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT, Bailhongal (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants, who are the wife and children of the deceased Mohan A Bendigeri, filed a claim petition under NC: 2023:KHC-D:7540-DB Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of deceased Mohan A Bendigeri that took place on 27.10.2016 involving TVS Excel Motorcycle bearing registration Nos.KA-22/EJ-0955 and VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D-1398.

It is stated that the deceased was aged 56 years as on the date of accident and he was working as Attender in the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Karnataka and drawing a salary of Rs.25,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Respondent No.1- Owner of VRL Bus contended that due to rash and negligent riding of rider of TVS Excel i.e. deceased, the accident took place and there was no fault on the part of driver of VRL bus.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company contended that liability is subject to terms and conditions of policy.
It was contended that due to rash and negligent riding of rider of motorcycle, the alleged accident had taken place.

Further it NC:
2023:KHC-D:7540-DB contended that the driver of VRL bus was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, 1st claimant-wife of the deceased examined as PW1 and also examined one eye- witness as PW2 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P14.
On behalf of the respondents, no witnesses were examined, but respondent No.2 got marked policy of insurance as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal based on the material evidence on record awarded total compensation of Rs.17,40,352/- with interest at 9% per annum on the following heads:
 Loss of Dependency Rs.16,55,352/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 60,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 25,000/-

While awarding the above compensation, Tribunal assessed income of the deceased at Rs.22,991/- per month, deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and applied multiplier of 9 taking the age of the deceased as 56 years.
The claimants not being satisfied with NC: 2023:KHC-D:7540-DB the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal are before this Court praying for enhancement of compensation.

7. Heard Sri. Sharad M Patil, learned counsel for appellants-claimants as well as Sri.Rajashekhar S Arani, learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company and perused the appeal papers.
8.
Sri. Sharad M Patil, learned counsel for the appellants-claimants advanced twofold contentions.

Firstly, he would submit that in the light of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1, the claimants would be entitled to an addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects, wherever the deceased was in a permanent job and in the age group of 50 to 60 years.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the only point that would fall for consideration in this appeal is, whether the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?
11. Our answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons.

12. The occurrence of the accident on 27.10.2016 involving TVS Excel Motorcycle bearing registration Nos.KA- 22/EJ-0955 and VRL Bus bearing registration No.KA-25/D- 1398 and resultant death of deceased Mohan A Bendigeri is 2018 ACJ 2782 NC: 2023:KHC-D:7540-DB not in dispute in this appeal.
The monthly income assessed by the Tribunal based on Ex.P12-Salary Certificate, which needs no interference.
It is the contention of the claimants that the Tribunal committed an error in not adding 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

In the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that wherever the deceased had a permanent job and was in the age group of 50 to 60 years, the claimants would be entitled for addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.
In the instant case, the deceased was aged 56 years and was in permanent employment working as Attender in Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Karnataka.
Therefore, the claimants would be entitled for addition of 15% of the assessed income towards future prospects.

Deduction of 1/3rd taken by the Tribunal towards personal and living expenses of the deceased is not disturbed, which is just and proper.
Proper multiplier applicable to the age of the deceased is '9'.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for compensation on the head of NC: 2023:KHC-D:7540-DB loss of dependency at Rs.19,03,655/-
(Rs.22,991 + 15% x 12 x 9 x 2/3).
13.

It is well settled law that the claimants being wife and children of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal and parental consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra).

As held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate,
besides Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.

Thus, claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
Sl. No. Particulars Amount  1. Loss of dependency Rs.19,03,655/-
 (Rs.22,991 (income) + Rs.3448.65  (15% future prospects) =26439.65  x 12 (months) x 9 (multiplier) x  2/3 (1/3rd deduction) =
 Rs.19,03,654.8 Rounded off to  Rs.19,03,655/-
 2. Loss of estate & Funeral Rs. 30,000/-
 expenses 3. Spousal & Parental Consortium Rs. 1,20,000/-
 (Rs.40,000/- each)
 Total Rs.20,53,655/-

15. In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
a) The above appeal is allowed in part.

b) The impugned judgment & award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.20,53,655/- as against Rs.17,40,352/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:7540-DB e) Apportionment, deposit & disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
f) Draw modified award accordingly.
